title: Grothendieck generators for quasi-coherent sheaves on an arbitrary scheme
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For every scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme], let $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ be the full category of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaves [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ is Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Its inclusion in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ is exact and creates all small colimits: the colimit in module sheaves of any small diagram of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent and is its colimit in $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$. In particular there is an object $G_X\in\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ such that $\operatorname{Hom}(G_X,-)$ is faithful, and filtered colimits are exact. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 077P, proposition-coherator, part (1) and its proof: all colimits agree with module-sheaf colimits and a generator is constructed from the set of bounded-cardinality quasi-coherent objects. Exactness of the inclusion is the abelian subcategory assertion in schemes.tex, section-quasi-coherent.

proof.text: Let $D:J\to\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ be any small diagram and let $C$ be its colimit in module sheaves, which exists by [lem-pc-scheme-modules-grothendieck-abelian]. On an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, restriction preserves this colimit by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. Put $M_j=\Gamma(U,D_j|_U)$ and $M=\operatorname{colim}_jM_j$, which exists by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian]. The natural counits $\widetilde M_j\cong D_j|_U$ and preservation of all small colimits by tilde, both clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], identify $C|_U$ with $\widetilde M$. This is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Thus $C$ is quasi-coherent by the affine-local definition [pqf-def-coherent]. Since the subcategory is full, the ambient universal Hom bijections for $C$ restrict to the same bijections for quasi-coherent targets. This proves that the inclusion creates all small colimits, including zero objects and finite biproducts.

source.place: Tag 01ID, lemma-colimit-quasi-coherent; Tag 01LA, section-quasi-coherent, (1)-(4); Tag 01IB, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent. This is the colimit assertion used in Tag 077P, proof of (1).

proof.text: For a map between quasi-coherent objects, its ambient kernel is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel], and its ambient cokernel and image are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image]. Fullness restricts their universal properties to $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$. Addition of maps is inherited; zero and finite biproducts were obtained in step 1. The ambient category is abelian by [lem-pc-scheme-modules-grothendieck-abelian]. These closure properties are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-full-subcategory-exact], which gives abelianness, the inherited kernels and cokernels, and equivalence of short exactness with ambient short exactness. In particular the inclusion is exact.

source.place: Tags 01IC, lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent, and 01LA, section-quasi-coherent, (5); the full abelian subcategory argument using these kernels and cokernels.

proof.text: For a small filtered diagram of short exact sequences in $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$, step 2 makes it a diagram of ambient short exact sequences. By [lem-pc-scheme-modules-grothendieck-abelian], its ambient colimit sequence is exact. Step 1 identifies each of its three colimit objects and the induced maps with those in $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$. Step 2 then reflects this exactness back into $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$. Thus filtered colimits are exact.

source.place: Tag 01AH, lemma-limits-colimits, (3), as used in Tag 077P, proposition-coherator, proof of (1).

proof.text:
Choose $\kappa$ as in [lem-sfb-qcoh-bounded-submodule-union]. Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-generated-module-isoclasses] to $(|X|,\mathcal O_X)$ and this infinite cardinal. Retain the subset $T$ of representatives which are quasi-coherent: every $\kappa$-generated quasi-coherent object is represented because quasi-coherence is invariant under isomorphism by its local definition [pqf-def-coherent]. Define $G_X= igoplus_{t\in T}\mathcal M_t$, which is quasi-coherent by step 1. To check faithfulness, take distinct maps $f,g:\mathcal F	o\mathcal H$. The canonical inclusions $i_N:N	o\mathcal F$ from the small directed system in [lem-sfb-qcoh-bounded-submodule-union] are jointly epimorphic: equality after every $i_N$ would give equality by its colimit universal property. Choose $N$ with $fi_N
e gi_N$ and an isomorphism $a:\mathcal M_t\xrightarrow{\sim}N$. The coproduct universal property gives $p_t:G_X	o\mathcal M_t$ whose component on the $t$th summand is the identity and whose other components are zero. Set $h=i_Na p_t$. Composing $fh$ and $gh$ with the $t$th summand inclusion gives $fi_Na
e gi_Na$, so $fh
e gh$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(G_X,-)$ is faithful. All indexing sets and the cardinal belong to the fixed universes; no cover was required to be finite and no intersection of affine opens was required to be affine.

source.place: Tag 077P, proposition-coherator, proof of (1), generator construction from Tags 077N and 077M; the assertion that the coproduct is a generator is expanded using the two universal properties.

proof.text: Steps 1 and 2 give an abelian category with all small colimits, step 3 gives exact filtered colimits, and step 4 gives a generator. These are exactly the conditions of [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. The additional assertions about the inclusion and the faithful Hom functor have already been proved. No hypothesis on $X$ beyond being a scheme was used.

source.place: Tag 077P, proposition-coherator, (1), and the definition of a Grothendieck abelian category.
